description: Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is a comforting and nutritious Middle Eastern staple, beloved for its simple yet profound flavors. This hearty vegan soup combines red lentils with aromatic vegetables, bright lemon, and often a touch of earthy cumin. Perfect for a light meal or a warming appetizer, it embodies the essence of Lebanese home cooking.

instructions.title: Prepare Vegetables
instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add chopped onion and carrot, cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.

instructions.title: Add Aromatics and Spices
instructions.text: Stir in minced garlic, cumin powder, and turmeric powder. Cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to burn the garlic.

instructions.title: Combine Lentils and Liquid
instructions.text: Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot, then pour in the vegetable broth or water. Stir well to combine all ingredients, ensuring nothing sticks to the bottom.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have mostly broken down. Stir occasionally.

instructions.title: Blend and Season
instructions.text: For a smoother soup, carefully use an immersion blender to blend a portion or all of the soup to your desired consistency. Alternatively, mash some of the lentils with the back of a spoon. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

instructions.title: Finish with Lemon
instructions.text: Remove the pot from heat and stir in the fresh lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed, adding more lemon juice, salt, or pepper if desired for a balanced flavor.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Ladle the hot soup into bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and serve immediately with a drizzle of olive oil and a lemon wedge on the side. Enjoy with warm pita bread or crunchy croutons.

tips: For an extra layer of depth, add a bay leaf to the soup while simmering and remove it before blending or serving.
If you prefer a thicker soup, reduce the amount of liquid slightly or simmer uncovered for a few extra minutes. If too thick, add a splash more broth or water.
Adas soup tastes even better the next day! Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days and reheat gently on the stovetop.
article:
Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas, often simply called Adas, is a beloved staple across the Middle East, cherished for its comforting warmth, vibrant flavor, and incredible nutritional value. This humble yet hearty soup transcends mere sustenance, offering a taste of home and tradition in every spoonful. Whether you're seeking a nourishing meal on a cold day, a healthy lunch option, or a flavorful starter, this classic Middle Eastern dish is a culinary journey you won't want to miss. In this comprehensive guide, we'll delve into the essence of this soup, provide a detailed recipe, and share expert tips to help you master the art of making the perfect Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas. Get ready to discover why this bright, zesty, and utterly satisfying soup holds such a special place in regional cuisine.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas?

At its heart, Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is a simple yet profoundly flavorful soup made primarily from red lentils, fresh vegetables, aromatic spices, and a generous squeeze of lemon juice. "Adas" is the Arabic word for lentils, and in Lebanon, this particular preparation highlights the quick-cooking, naturally creamy red lentils. Unlike some heartier lentil stews, Adas is typically blended to a smooth, velvety consistency, making it incredibly appealing and easy to digest.

This soup is a cornerstone of Lebanese home cooking, often prepared year-round but especially popular during colder months or as a light Iftar meal during Ramadan. It's naturally vegan and gluten-free, making it an excellent choice for a variety of dietary preferences. The combination of earthy lentils with sautéed onions, carrots, and potatoes, brightened by cumin and turmeric, and finished with a crucial burst of fresh lemon juice and a drizzle of olive oil, creates a symphony of flavors that is both deeply satisfying and refreshingly light. Its characteristic vibrant orange-red hue is as inviting as its aroma, promising a bowl full of warmth and goodness.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting authentic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas requires a few key ingredients, most of which are likely already in your pantry. The quality of your produce and spices will significantly impact the final flavor, so opt for fresh ingredients whenever possible.

For a batch serving 6-8 people, you will need:

*   **1 ½ cups (300g) Red Lentils:** Rinsed thoroughly. These cook quickly and break down easily, creating the soup's signature creamy texture.
*   **2 tablespoons Olive Oil:** For sautéing the aromatics. Extra virgin olive oil is preferred for its flavor.
*   **1 large Yellow Onion:** Diced, forming the aromatic base.
*   **2 medium Carrots:** Peeled and diced, adding sweetness and depth.
*   **1 medium Potato:** Peeled and diced (e.g., Russet or Yukon Gold), contributing to the soup's body and creaminess.
*   **3-4 cloves Garlic:** Minced, for a pungent aroma.
*   **8 cups (2 liters) Vegetable Broth or Water:** Vegetable broth will add more flavor, but water works well too, especially if you plan to season heavily.
*   **1 teaspoon Ground Cumin:** Essential for its warm, earthy Middle Eastern flavor profile.
*   **½ teaspoon Ground Turmeric (optional):** Enhances the soup's vibrant color and adds a subtle earthy note.
*   **1 teaspoon Salt:** Or to taste.
*   **½ teaspoon Black Pepper:** Or to taste.
*   **¼ cup (60ml) Fresh Lemon Juice:** The star ingredient that brightens and balances all the flavors. Add at the very end.
*   **Fresh Mint Leaves:** For garnish and a burst of freshness.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** For drizzling over the finished soup.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these simple steps to create a delicious pot of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Place the red lentils in a fine-mesh sieve and rinse them thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and excess starch. Set aside.

2.  **Sauté the Aromatics:** In a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat the 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion, carrots, and potato. Sauté for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables begin to soften and the onion becomes translucent.

3.  **Add Garlic and Spices:** Stir in the minced garlic, ground cumin, and turmeric (if using). Cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn the garlic.

4.  **Combine with Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed lentils to the pot, stirring them in with the sautéed vegetables. Pour in the vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

5.  **Simmer and Cook:** Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

6.  **Blend the Soup:** Carefully remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until it reaches your desired smooth and creamy consistency. Alternatively, you can carefully transfer batches of the soup to a regular blender (fill only halfway, hold the lid firmly, and vent the top to release steam) and blend until smooth. Return the blended soup to the pot.

7.  **Season and Finish:** Return the pot to low heat. Stir in the fresh lemon juice, salt, and black pepper. Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed. You might want more salt or a little extra lemon juice for brightness.

8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas into bowls. Drizzle each serving with a swirl of extra virgin olive oil and garnish generously with fresh mint leaves. Serve immediately.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving the perfect bowl of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is simple with a few expert tricks:

*   **Rinse Your Lentils Thoroughly:** This step is crucial. Rinsing removes impurities and extra starch, which can make your soup cloudy or gummy. Don't skip it!
*   **Build Flavor from the Start:** Sautéing your onions, carrots, and potatoes until tender and slightly caramelized before adding liquids creates a rich, flavorful base for your soup. Don't rush this step.
*   **Don't Skimp on Lemon:** Fresh lemon juice is perhaps the most critical ingredient in Adas. It adds a vibrant tang that cuts through the richness of the lentils and brightens the entire soup. Add it at the very end to preserve its fresh, zesty flavor. Taste and adjust – some prefer more lemon than others.
*   **Blend to Perfection:** An immersion blender is your best friend for this soup, making blending easy and mess-free. If using a regular blender, be extremely cautious with hot liquids. Blend until smooth, but you can leave a slightly chunkier texture if you prefer a less uniform soup.
*   **Season as You Go (and at the End):** While you add salt and pepper during cooking, always taste and adjust the seasoning just before serving. The flavors intensify as the soup sits, and the final lemon addition might require a tweak to the salt.
*   **Use Good Quality Olive Oil:** A drizzle of high-quality extra virgin olive oil over the finished soup not only adds a lovely sheen but also a rich, fruity flavor that enhances the overall experience.

## Serving Suggestions

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is wonderfully versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways:

*   **As a Main Course:** Paired with warm pita bread or crusty bread for dipping, it makes a light yet satisfying meal on its own.
*   **As an Appetizer:** Serve smaller portions as a comforting starter to a larger Middle Eastern feast.
*   **With Garnishes:** Beyond fresh mint and olive oil, consider a sprinkle of sumac for extra tang, a pinch of red pepper flakes for a gentle kick, or homemade croutons for added crunch. Lemon wedges on the side allow each diner to adjust the tartness to their liking.
*   **Alongside:** A simple side salad, olives, or pickles can complement the soup beautifully, adding contrasting textures and flavors.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas recipe is perfect as is, there are several ways to adapt it to your taste or what you have on hand:

*   **Add More Vegetables:** Feel free to incorporate other quick-cooking vegetables like diced celery, zucchini, or even a handful of fresh spinach or Swiss chard towards the end of the cooking process. Sweet potato can be used instead of regular potato for a slightly sweeter flavor.
*   **Spice It Up:** For a subtle smokiness, add a pinch of smoked paprika. A tiny amount of cayenne pepper or a fresh chili can introduce a pleasant warmth if you enjoy a bit of heat. A dash of coriander can also complement the cumin.
*   **Different Garnishes:** While mint is traditional, fresh parsley or cilantro can also be used. Toasted pine nuts or slivered almonds can add a delightful crunch.
*   **Broth Alternatives:** If you're not strictly vegetarian or vegan, chicken broth can be used instead of vegetable broth or water for a richer flavor base.
*   **Texture Control:** For a thinner soup, simply add more broth or water until it reaches your desired consistency. For a thicker soup, you can reduce the amount of liquid slightly or simmer it uncovered for a few extra minutes after blending.
*   **Make it a Heartier Meal:** While not traditional for Adas, you could stir in a can of drained chickpeas after blending for added protein and texture, creating more of a stew-like consistency.

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas is more than just a recipe; it's an invitation to experience a culinary tradition rooted in warmth, hospitality, and wholesome goodness. This vibrant, nutritious, and incredibly flavorful soup is remarkably easy to prepare, making it a perfect addition to any home cook's repertoire. Whether you're seeking comfort, health, or simply a delicious meal, this classic Middle Eastern dish promises to deliver. So gather your ingredients, follow our steps, and prepare to savor the delightful taste of authentic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup Adas – a truly timeless bowl of joy.
